I am old now, seventy-one years, and my strength is not what it was. This plot by my house is all I have, so I must look after it well. If the coupon comes to me this year, I will use the fertilizer and the good seed on my maize, because without them the harvest is too small to feed me. I put the goat manure I have saved onto the ridges before the rains, and I ask my grandchildren to help me weed — sometimes I pay a young man from the village a little maize to help me dig the ridges, because my back cannot do it all.
